title: Jasmine Tea and Rose Sorbet
changes_from_base: Jasmine tea pearls, rose petals and a little star anise steeped below boiling replace the fruit; coconut milk is an optional serving broth.
summary: A delicate, floral sorbet of jasmine tea and rose petals steeped below boiling, with a hint of lime and star anise.

ingredients.item: whole star anise, broken in half
light corn syrup or glucose syrup

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.text: Warm it to about 80 °C, just steaming with small bubbles on the base. Never let it boil, now or later, or the tea turns bitter.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Put the sugar, jasmine pearls, rose petals and star anise in the saucepan, pour on the hot water and stir until the sugar dissolves. Keep on the lowest heat for 10 min.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the sieve into a jug, stir in the corn syrup, lime juice and zest, then cool.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate overnight, or until very cold.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min, then freeze for 2-3 h until set.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: For a simple coconut broth, spoon 2 tbsp coconut milk into each small bowl and add two small scoops of sorbet.

tips: Keep the water below boiling at every stage or the tea will taste bitter.
If you cannot find rose petals, stir 1 tsp rose water into the cooled tea instead.
Small cooked tapioca pearls in the coconut milk make it a fuller dessert.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 1 week; sorbet turns icy after that. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
